issues.description: IAM scan is sequential per image; a filter-shaped helper would compose better.
issues.detail: _get_images iterates images and calls getIamPolicy one-by-one inside the listing loop. The data flow is image -> policy -> public_flag, a classic stateless transform. Extracting a small _is_publicly_shared(project, name) helper would let the listing loop stay flat and make the algorithm self-evident. Not blocking; just cleaner composition.

issues.description: publicly_shared on Image bakes the check verdict into the data structure.
issues.detail: The Image model stores a precomputed boolean derived from one specific check's policy. The right data shape is the raw IAM members (or a small set of public principals); the check can then derive its own verdict. This would let future checks (e.g. allUsers if ever permitted, role-specific exposure) reuse the same data without service edits.

issues.description: CHANGELOG and PR description name the check differently than the metadata.
issues.detail: CHANGELOG lists compute_image_not_publicly_shared while the PR description repeatedly says compute_image_publicly_shared. Both point at the same directory, but the inconsistent naming will bite grep-driven maintenance. Pick one name and use it everywhere; data (identifiers) should be unambiguous.

issues.description: Exception swallowing in _get_images conflates listing and policy failures.
issues.detail: The inner try logs a getIamPolicy failure and silently treats the image as not-public. That's a policy decision hidden in error handling; an image whose IAM is unreadable is not the same as one that's safe. Consider a tri-state (unknown) or an explicit failure surface so the check can decide rather than the service inventing data.

issues.description: Test for id type uses .__class__.__name__ == 'str' instead of isinstance.
issues.detail: Minor, but the test asserts the class name string rather than the type. isinstance(x, str) says exactly what's meant and survives subclassing. Small cleverness with no payoff.

review.summary: The change is small, composable, and follows the existing GCP service/check pattern well. Data shape is the main thing worth a second look: storing publicly_shared on the Image bakes one check's verdict into the model, and swallowing getIamPolicy errors as "not public" lets the service invent data on the check's behalf. A tiny extracted helper for the policy-to-flag transform would make the listing loop read as a filter. Naming drift between CHANGELOG (compute_image_not_publicly_shared) and the PR description (compute_image_publicly_shared) should be reconciled. No correctness blockers.
